videos.title: The Settings space
videos.intro: Settings is where the hotel is set up. In this video you will see the Settings space, its menu, and who sees what.

scenes.say: Click Settings in the switcher at the top. Settings is a space of its own, with its own menu.
Back to front office, at the top of the menu, takes you back to the hotel's daily work.
The menu has nine groups, starting with Property. A group shows only when it holds something you may open.
An entry with a small arrow opens a Front office screen. Cancellation terms is one.
Then come Rooms, Rates and tax, Money, Lists, Front desk, Messages, People and security, and Modules and connections.
Settings is for the owner, an Admin and the GM. A page changes the hotel chosen in the top bar, so check it first.
The GM sees a little less. Under People and security: People, Audit log, Activity and Signing in.
Under Modules and connections there is no Modules page and no Integrations. Those are for the owner and an Admin.
Many switches in Settings save the moment you tap them, with no Save button. Change them only when you mean to.

videos.outro: That is the Settings space. The next videos take each group in turn, starting with the hotel's profile.

videos.title: The hotel's profile
videos.intro: This video is for the owner, an Admin and the GM: the Profile page, where the hotel's details and numbers are kept.

scenes.say: Profile is the first page in Settings. While something is missing, a yellow card at the top says what the hotel still needs before it can take a guest.
It counts the checks that are settled: here, eight of ten. Nothing on it is ticked by hand; the system checks each line itself.
A line like this one blocks: until it is settled, a booking, a bill or the night audit will refuse and say so. Here, the GST number is still the standard dummy number.
A line marked not blocking is worth doing, but stops nothing. Tap any line to open the screen that settles it.
Below, the Profile card holds what prints on the hotel's invoices. Tap Edit to change it.
The code is in every address and every invoice number. It cannot be changed.
The hotel's name is the group owner's. For anybody else, this box is locked.
The GST number is fifteen characters, the two-digit state code first. It prints on every invoice.
Change what is wrong, and tap Save.
Lower down is the food safety licence number. Tap Change and type the fourteen digits from the licence; it prints on food bills.
More registration numbers keeps up to four others, each with its own name. They are kept here, never printed.
Tap Add, type the name and the number, then Save.

videos.outro: When every check is settled, the yellow card goes by itself. It comes back if anything stops being true.

videos.title: Logo, photos, highlights and amenities
videos.intro: In this video you will set what the hotel shows: its logo on its documents, and its photos, texts and amenities on the guest's own page.

scenes.say: On Logo and photos, this hotel's logo prints on its bills and documents, in place of the group's logo.
Tap Upload and choose a PNG or an SVG file, 200 kilobytes at most. The voucher prints a PNG logo.
Add photos puts up to twenty photos on the guest's page during the stay. Never a guest in one.
Highlights are five texts guests read about the hotel, one tab each: the property, local attractions, directions, activities nearby and famous landmarks.
Type in plain words; a blank line starts a new paragraph. A text left blank is not shown.
Tap Save on each text.
Amenities is one list for every hotel in the group. Switch on what this hotel has, and guests see it on their page.
The list itself is kept by the owner and an Admin. Add puts a new amenity on it, for every hotel.
Find an amenity by typing part of its name.
The pencil renames it.
Turn Off takes it off for every hotel.
And the bin deletes it, but only while no hotel has it on.

videos.outro: Each room type picks its own amenities from the same list, as the room types video shows.

videos.title: The group and the policies
videos.intro: This video covers two pages under Property: Group, and Policies.

scenes.say: The group's name and logo are one for every hotel. Every bill prints the hotel's name, then by, and the group's name.
Tap Change to type the group's name; blank means none. The group's logo prints at every hotel with no logo of its own.
Office details are the footer of every booking voucher. Until one is typed, a voucher's footer is the hotel's own.
On Policies, the house policies print on this hotel's booking voucher. Tap Edit, and type one policy a line, at most eight.
The policy texts are the hotel's own words on parking and arrival, families and extra guests, and the terms of a reservation. Each has its own Save.
Under Child ages, type up to what age a child stays free,
and up to what age a guest is a child.
Then Save. The ages are words only: prices do not change with them.
Cancellation terms, what a guest pays when they cancel, are set with the rates. This line opens that screen.

videos.outro: The house policies and the office details print on the vouchers from the moment they are saved.

videos.title: Room types and rooms
videos.intro: In this video you will add a room type and a room, and put the rooms in order.

scenes.say: Room types shows what the hotel sells, and the rooms it sells it in. No price is asked here: a new room type has none until it is priced on Rates.
To add a type, tap Add a room type.
Type a short code, two to ten letters or digits. It prints on the tape chart.
Then its name.
Adults the rate covers is how many the price is for, before an extra-person charge.
Sleeps at most is the most people the room takes. The details below it are optional.
Tap Save.
Edit opens a room type. Basic holds its numbers and words,
Amenities ticks what it has, from the group's list,
and Photos takes up to ten pictures of it.
Remove is only for a room type with no rooms, bookings or prices. One in use is switched off instead, by unticking Sold at this property.
To add a room, tap Add a room.
Type its number, at most ten letters and digits.
Choose its type. Type the floor, or leave it blank if the hotel has one floor.
Tick Smoking room if it is one, and Save.
Drag a room to put the rooms in order. Tap a room to change it, or untick Sellable to take it out of the house.
Import brings in room types, and then rooms, from a file.

videos.outro: Nothing in use is ever deleted. A room type or a room is switched off instead, and its history stays.

videos.title: Rate plans and meal plans
videos.intro: Prices are set on Rates, in the Front office. In this video you will see how rate plans and meal plans offer those prices.

scenes.say: Rate plans lists each room type on each meal plan, named by itself, such as Superior, Room only.
The master is the base room on room only. A derived plan follows it; an independent plan has its own base, typed on Rates.
Each plan says how it is priced.
And its price for two guests on the business date. A dash means it is not priced.
Switch a plan off and it is not offered for new bookings. Its prices and bookings stay.
Tap Edit to change a plan.
The editor has three steps. Step one says what the plan is; step two, its price.
Choose how it is priced. A derived plan asks how much more than the master, in rupees or percent.
The summary follows your choices.
Tap Next. Step three ticks the booking sources that sell it, none meaning every source. Then tap Update.
Meal plans says on which days each meal is served. Here, the breakfast plan.
Tick each meal on the check-in day, the stay-over days and the check-out day.
Then Save. The days show on the plan's summary and on the guest's voucher.

videos.outro: A meal's price is its add-on, on Rates. One price is set there, and every plan follows it.

videos.title: Taxes
videos.intro: In this video you will set the GST rules. One set of rules serves the front desk and the till.

scenes.say: Taxes has a heading for each kind of sale: rooms, restaurant, bar, banquet, spa, laundry and everything else. Alcohol has its own, where the hotel serves it.
A heading can have more than one rate. Here, a higher rate applies above a figure.
The SAC code prints on each line of this kind. Your accountant gives it.
A heading with no rate says Not set, with a dash, never a zero. Nothing under it can be billed until a rate is set.
To set or change a heading's rates, tap Edit, or Set it.
One row is one rate. Leave the first row's figure at zero, so it applies to everything.
Type its GST percent.
To charge more above a figure, add a second row with the figure and its rate. A row may also have dates, and a note saying why.
Then Save.
Lower down is the till's half: which heading each part of the menu sells under.
Choose the heading for each section. A dish under a heading with no rate is refused at the till.

videos.outro: No rate is built in. Every rate here is the hotel's own, confirmed by its accountant.

videos.title: Bank details and payment methods
videos.intro: In this video you will set the hotel's bank details, and the ways guests may pay.

scenes.say: Bank details print on the hotel's booking voucher; with none set, it prints none. The group's owner is told whenever they change.
Type the name the account is in.
Then the account number, digits only.
The bank, the branch, and the I F S C: eleven characters, the fifth a zero.
A UPI ID, if guests may pay to one.
Then Save.
Payment methods is how guests pay here: what the bill, New booking and a function's bill offer.
Each method is on or off, and the switch saves at once. One that is off is not offered or taken.
The default is what the desk's payment screens start on. To change it, open a method and tap Make default.
The pencil edits a method.
The bin shows only for a method never used.
To add one, tap Add a method.
Its name is what the bill and the receipt print.
In the books is where the reports count it. A booking site that collected the money is Bill to company, owed by that site in the city ledger.
Tap Save.

videos.outro: The default way of paying also shows on Times and rules, in the Front desk group.

videos.title: Charges, discounts and commission
videos.intro: In this video you will set the extra charges, the named discounts, the commission, and pickup and drop.

scenes.say: Extra charges starts with the early check-in fee,
and the late check-out fee. Blank means no fee, never a zero.
Tap Save fees.
Below is the list of what a booking may add; the bill's Add charge picks from it. Tap Add a charge.
Type its name.
And its price. Leave it blank when the rate includes it at no charge, such as a welcome drink.
The bill's column is where the money lands in the reports: a cake under Food, a pickup under Other charges.
This switch marks a pickup or a drop.
Then Save.
Discounts are named discounts on rooms, for New booking. By hand the desk may give up to ten percent of a night, with a reason; more only by picking one of these.
Type its name,
choose percent or rupees,
type how much off each night, and Save.
Commission is what each booking source takes. Blank means no commission agreed: a dash, not zero.
Type a source's percent,
and Save that row. A change applies to bookings made after it.
Pickup and drop holds the airport, station and bus stand runs. The time goes in the booking's note.

videos.outro: On each of these lists, the switch turns one on or off, the pencil edits it, and the bin shows only for one never used.

videos.title: The lists
videos.intro: The lists are what the desk picks from instead of typing. In this video you will see how every list works.

scenes.say: Market segments say who the guest is, for the reports. They are offered on New booking.
Search finds one.
Type a new one, and tap Add.
The arrows move it up or down.
Tap a name to rename it. A booking keeps the words it was made with.
The tick switches it on or off.
The bin deletes it. One that a booking uses cannot be deleted, only switched off.
Reservation types are the Calendar's colours for each kind of booking. Tap a colour to choose another.
Back to the built-in colours puts them all back.
Ready reasons are what the desk taps instead of typing: for a block, a cancel, a void, and a bill correction.
Type a new reason and add it. Typing your own reason at the desk still works.
For a holiday, choose the day,
type its name, pick a colour, and tap Add. The Calendar and Rates shade it like a weekend; no price reads it.
ID types are the documents the hotel takes. One switched off leaves the check-in, New booking and the guest's online form.
VIP levels are one list for the whole group, because a guest is one record at every hotel. Only the owner or an Admin changes it.

videos.outro: Booking sources, the first entry under Lists, opens its own Front office screen.

videos.title: The front desk's times and rules
videos.intro: In this video you will set the front desk's hours, and the rules its screens start on.

scenes.say: Times and rules has two cards: the front desk's hours, and its rules.
The early arrival and late departure fees show here; a dash means none.
Edit opens the hours.
Type when rooms are ready from,
and when they are due back. A guest earlier or later needs a reason and somebody to allow it.
The fees themselves are set on Extra charges, under Money.
In the rules card, Way of paying is the default payment method, set on Payment methods.
Edit opens the rules.
Advance before check-in: none, the first night, or the whole stay. It is never asked of a company's booking, or one prepaid on a booking site.
With The desk may overbook off, a booking past a full house is refused.
The weekend days are shaded on the Calendar and Rates. No price reads them.
The Front desk rules page goes further, and each choice saves the moment it is made. A new booking starts as confirmed or tentative, billed to the guest or a company.
Tick what a booking must carry; New booking will not save without it. A booking from a booking site is never held for it.
Housekeeping decides which rooms are sent for cleaning, besides every room left at check-out.
The restaurant's round-off is manual, automatic, or off. Room bills and invoices are never rounded.
How the figures count explains occupancy, ADR and RevPAR in plain words.
Two switches decide whether a complimentary room counts as sold, and whether a day use counts as half a room.

videos.outro: The desk can still change a new booking's guarantee and bill-to, booking by booking.

videos.title: Guest messages and report emails
videos.intro: In this video you will choose which messages guests get by themselves, and who gets the daily reports.

scenes.say: This page lists each message a guest gets by itself. The booking voucher goes once, when a booking is confirmed, on WhatsApp and by email.
Its switch saves at once, for this hotel only.
Online check-in puts the guest's check-in link and QR code in the voucher. The review request goes when a clerk presses Ask for a review.
The tax invoice goes by email when it is issued, but only for invoices issued after it is switched on.
Daily report emails go right after the night audit closes the day. Here, nothing is sent yet: sending is not set up on the server.
There are four reports, each with its own switch. The night audit report starts on; the others start off.
Type who gets it, one email address a line, and tap Save at the foot. Nobody gets anything until an address is typed.

videos.outro: Guest messages, Reviews and Online check-in, with their small arrows, open their own Front office screens.

videos.title: People and security
videos.intro: This video covers People and security: who may do what, who did what, and how people sign in.

scenes.say: People, the first entry, opens the Front office screen where people are added. For the owner, Add somebody has a Test switch: that person works only in a test hotel, made on Properties.
Roles and permissions shows the fourteen roles. It is read only.
Each row says what each role may do. The menus, the buttons and the server all read this same table.
The audit log is the money's record. Nothing in it is edited or deleted: a wrong posting is reversed, and the reversal is its own entry.
Find entries by part of a name,
or between two dates.
Older and Newer turn the pages.
Activity is every change: who made it, when, and to which record.
Across the group shows changes that belong to no single hotel. It is for the owner and an Admin.
Choose one person,
or one kind of record.
What changed shows each field, from and to. A guest's details only read changed.
Sign-ins and devices shows when each person signed in, and on what device, for ninety days. Sign out this device makes that device sign in again.
Signing in states the rules. A password is at least ten characters for the owner, an Admin and a GM, and at least eight for everybody else.

videos.outro: Two-step sign-in, for the owner, Admins and GMs, comes after this release.

videos.title: Modules and connections
videos.intro: This last video covers Modules and connections: what the hotel runs, and its outside connections.

scenes.say: Modules is for the owner and an Admin only. Each module is a part of the system this property runs, such as Point of sale.
Its switch saves at once. For most, off means the screens go and the server refuses them.
Reception can use the P O S lets Reception take, bill and settle orders at the till. Off hides it from Reception only.
Rivals' prices checks nearby hotels' lowest prices on Google Hotels, twice a week, for the next thirty nights. Nothing here changes a price.
Here the server has no search key yet, so nothing is checked.
Connection health lists every outside connection: emails, WhatsApp, the CRS, sign-in, backups and rivals' prices.
Each says Working, Needs a look, Not working, or Not set up.
And when it last worked. Nothing is changed here: a connection is set up on the server.

videos.outro: Channel manager, CRS bookings and Integrations open their own Front office screens. That is Settings. Thank you for watching.
